Perastage Canonical MVR contract

Perastage Canonical MVR is the standards-valid MVR 1.6 representation of the current domain scene. Project scene.mvr, MVR-xchange, and read-only consumers use CanonicalMvrExportOptions() and the same serializer. The canonical truss representation is the standard MVR Symbol/Symdef representation. Every normal standalone export uses this policy, independently of saved compatibility preferences.

For an explicit Direct Geometry3D for truss symbols standalone export, the same serializer derives a compatibility representation from a private copy of the canonical scene. It expands supported Symbol/Symdef truss geometry into direct Geometry3D references without changing the live scene. This is an alternative standards-valid MVR 1.6 serialization: a Truss requires Geometries, whose graphical children may be either Symbol or Geometry3D. The option improves interoperability with applications whose Symbol/Symdef support is incomplete, but it is never project persistence, canonical snapshot, MVR-xchange, Inspector, or internal scene authority.

The canonical root contains at most one GeneralSceneDescription/UserData. That element contains one Data provider="Perastage" ver="1.0" block. Its versioned maps supplement scene fidelity, including fixture type information, ProjectFixtureMetadataMap, truss and hoist information, primitive geometry, and layer appearance. These maps never replace an official MVR or GDTF field and never contain local absolute paths. Supported Perastage fixture metadata is applied by project restore, replace/open, and merge imports. Entries are keyed to fixture UUIDs; the existing merge remapping then carries each imported fixture and its restored values to its collision-free identity without changing unrelated target objects. Unsupported versions and malformed entries remain non-fatal diagnostics.

Valid foreign root Data blocks are stored separately as opaque scene data. Perastage does not interpret them. Canonical export reparses each stored block, diagnoses and rejects malformed or misplaced payloads, omits anything claiming Perastage ownership, deduplicates repeated payloads, and places accepted blocks beside the single Perastage block under the one legal root UserData. Merge unions these blocks without accumulating duplicates. XML subtree serialization may normalize insignificant formatting, but preserves provider identity and XML structure.

MvrExporter::ExportCanonicalSnapshotToBuffer copies the supplied MvrScene and performs identity and transform recovery only on that copy. Snapshot and normal serialization therefore cannot mark the live project dirty or leak repairs into it. Resource leases are shared by the copy, avoiding duplication of resource payloads while keeping their lifetime safe.

Interactive project save and standalone export both call SyncSceneData() as an explicit command-boundary preparation step. This commits pending derived fixture type colors to the domain scene without reintroducing table-wide GUI resynchronization. Project save then requests the canonical policy. File > Export MVR starts with Use compatibility export for this file unchecked. The saved preference suggests the representation only after that explicit opt-in; it remains stored under its existing key. The dialog shows the transformation and passes explicit options to the same exporter. Cancelling or unavailable dialog customization leaves the canonical policy in effect. Direct Geometry3D derives only the standalone compatibility representation. Direct domain serialization and Inspector snapshots remain independent of GUI preferences and operate on the scene supplied by their caller.

The .pstg container continues to own application and workspace state outside scene.mvr: window perspectives, splitter positions, selections, preferences, toolbar state, caches, revision/dirty bookkeeping, and machine-specific paths. Only portable state that describes or supplements the scene belongs in MVR.

Layer UUIDs and object layerUuid ownership are authoritative. Names, including empty and duplicate names, are preserved independently; generated GUI labels never replace authored MVR names. The default layer has a canonical deterministic UUID before export. See Layer identity for default policy, legacy layer_default migration, workspace state, and compatibility boundaries.

Layer owns its MVR 1.6 vertical elevation and authored matrix precision. Scene node transforms are world-space; exported local matrices are relative to the immediate GroupObject or, for roots, the owning Layer. Import composes each parent once. Export preserves unedited numeric source values, repairs locals on a private snapshot after world-space edits, and may omit an identity Layer Matrix. Layer merge equality includes the authored matrix values. Non-elevation, malformed or ambiguous layer matrices remain fail-closed.

Fixture and Support each own one optional standard Addresses collection with ordered DMX Address and Network lists (Address children precede Network), retaining container presence, optional break attributes and authored values. Missing break means 0; break IDs identify assignments and never universes. Fixture.address is the compatibility projection of break 0 only. Unedited nonzero-only or out-of-editor- range assignments remain preservable without an invented primary assignment. Core perastage::patch::SetFixturePrimaryPatch edits only break 0. Explicit patching of an absent/empty list creates it; clearing removes only it and retains the container/other entries. A missing primary in a nonempty list, duplicate breaks or invalid values produces a structured conflict. Existing table/auto-patch workflows use that policy; auto-patch publication is atomic. Pending legacy scalar edits reconcile only on a private export snapshot with an unambiguous mapping. A final serialized projection check protects the complete ordered list. Fixture Network retains required case-sensitive GDTF wire-geometry names and optional ipv4/subnetmask/ipv6/dhcp/hostname presence and text. Patch edits never modify this list. Names are not UUID references and are not remapped at merge. Known-invalid or ambiguous GDTF references block publication; unavailable local GDTF evidence retains metadata without guessing and reports ResourceMissing at publication, preventing a dummy GDTF from invalidating wire references. Core rebind validation rejects unsafe definition changes before publishing. Support uses the same reference policy and XML assignment writer; its Addresses follow GDTFMode and precede FixtureID. Authored Support GDTF bindings also require an available resource and explicit mode, even without Network; a dangling mode cannot be omitted or replaced by Default. Malformed/unknown data, other address consumers and unsupported extensions remain guarded. Network geometry/hostname control whitespace also fails closed because the XML writer cannot retain its character-reference form. Fixture-to-Support conversion preserves the complete collection, Classing, standard identifiers (including CustomId/CustomIdType presence and explicit zero), GDTF binding, position, layer/group ownership and numeric matrix source. Legacy primary patch strings are materialized through the existing patch policy. Focus, Fixture Color, Pan/Tilt inversion, explicit project color/symbol/power overrides and retained source conflicts or missing required GDTF mode/binding return a structured field-specific refusal before mutation or Undo publication. Derived fixture metadata is not a new Support standard field; existing hoist load/function defaults remain intentional conversion semantics. No network settings are applied. Published Universe.Address strings and signed break IDs are preserved even where the unchanged pinned XSD's integer/nonnegative restrictions disagree.

Root UserData precedes Scene, as required by the official XSD. Every exported GroupObject retains ChildList, including empty groups, to satisfy the pinned XSD; published MVR 1.6 Table 22 permits its absence. These representation rules preserve standards-valid identity round-trips.

FocusPoint uses the existing geometric SceneObject value with a distinct SceneObjectKind::FocusPoint and is serialized with its standard element name. Direct geometry, ownership, transforms and Fixture Focus links share the existing identity/resource/mutation services. Symbol-based focus geometry still requires preservation support and blocks writes. A required Geometries container may be empty; no replacement mesh is invented for an empty focus.

Export preparation rejects durable known-loss evidence before identity/transform recovery or archive writing. PSTG and MVR-xchange snapshots use that same gate. This is bounded protection, not proof that every standard field survives. See the coverage audit for protected structures, unresolved P0 losses and the official XSD/UserData discrepancy. Full-document XSD conformance must not be inferred from the internal structural validator or from successful export/reimport.

Classes are a persistent scene-wide UUID registry, independent of layers. Each supported Fixture, GroupObject, FocusPoint, SceneObject, Truss and Support owns its optional direct Classing UUID. Export retains unused definitions and exact optional names; equal names never identify or coalesce classes. Merge remaps real identity collisions and incoming references together, including cross-kind collisions regardless of object replacement policy. Malformed/ambiguous source identities, dangling references or unrepresented class content remain blocked; a final projection check rejects serializer omissions before publication.

This preserves the identity model needed for future class visibility filtering across layers in Viewer2D, Viewer3D and Layout Mode. There are no visibility controls or flags in this change. Visibility presets and documentation settings will belong to PSTG, without adding proprietary Class attributes to MVR.

Preservation, canonicalization and controlled repair

Preservation protects valid authored information and meaning, including fields without an editor. Canonicalization may change representation: standard element ordering, equivalent numeric spelling, resource packaging with consistent reference rewriting, identity layer matrices, empty optional assignment containers, and required XSD containers. It does not authorize changing arbitrary text, precision, identities or relationships. XML whitespace in otherwise empty optional assignment containers, including character references, is insignificant; attributes, child elements and non-whitespace text remain protected. This is a bounded rule, not permission to discard unknown fields.

For the same scene and effective canonical options, PSTG scene.mvr and standalone canonical output must have exactly the same ordered ZIP entry names and uncompressed bytes, including XML text, attributes, values and element order. ZIP metadata and compression may differ. This compares two generated outputs, not generated output with imported XML. Project documentation, styles, visibility presets and preferences belong outside scene.mvr.

FixtureID and FixtureIDNumeric are selection labels, independent of persistent UUID identity. Authored duplicates, zero, empty strings and optional presence retain the bounded #2484 policy. Future allocation/duplicate repair must be an explicit reusable plan, with diagnostics and Undo/Redo when applied to the live scene. Import repair changes state at an explicit command boundary; canonical export only derives a private snapshot; compatibility export is a named alternate operation. None may consume future repair preferences implicitly.

UUID spelling/unique-alias recovery on a private export snapshot remains available and diagnosed. An ambiguous alias reported by identity recovery now returns IdentityConflict / Error / ExportFailed before transform preparation or serialization. No guessed or cleared reference is published. The lower-level recovery utility still exposes its historical recovery result and is not itself a general validation API. Generic source UUID/reference coverage, Position recovery and opaque provider references remain P0; this gate is not proof of complete reference preservation.

Safe representable content should save without a consent loop. Genuine unsupported standard content still blocks both serializers until an actual preservation owner exists. This is an unresolved workflow constraint, not the final product policy. No validation bypass, alternate project scene or lossy-save override is provided. The audit records the smallest proposed recovery design and acceptance conditions separately from implemented behavior.
